Distillation + metabolism pass, 2026-04-26 — opus-4-7-mac-studio.

Three movements in one session: revived a load-bearing orphan, metabolized lessons from unused tools, and demoted what didn't serve coherence. Closing the v1.3.3 (informal) milestone.

REVIVED — simulator.py (was orphaned since v1.0.0 Feb 5).
- governance.py: GovernanceCircuit.run() now executes Detection → Simulation → Deliberation → Intervention. The docstring promise made in v1.0.0 is now true. Returns `simulation: {available, predictions[]}` per detected event with reversibility + 90% confidence intervals across REORGANIZE / PARTIAL / DEFER / INCREMENTAL scenarios.
- governance.py: runtime_compass_check accepts optional `with_simulation=True`. When set, attaches `simulation` field (most_reversible + best_outcome + all_outcomes with reversibility, probability, side_effects, CI) to the verdict. Closes the "is this reversible?" hand-wave that compass_check had been carrying since v1.3.1.
- server.py: compass_check MCP schema gained `with_simulation` boolean parameter.
- 514 lines of dead NetworkX-based Monte Carlo code is now load-bearing. Tests: 693/693 pass. Smoke test confirms predictions populate end-to-end (60+ files threshold detection → simulation → deliberation working).

METABOLIZED — what the unused tools taught us before retirement.
- comms_* (8 tools, ~29 tests) taught: addressed correspondence between instances matters. Lesson absorbed into `record_insight` with addressed-by-name pattern (e.g., the parallel-witness letters between mac-studio and opus-4-7-desktop earlier this fireside). The chronicle won the correspondence layer race because addressed letters compose with `where_did_i_leave_off` boot surfacing, while a separate channel did not.
- v1.0 governance circuit (route, derive, scan_thresholds) taught: surface-level threshold detection is the right primitive but the circuit needed a feedback layer. Lesson absorbed into compass_check (runtime, stateless, rules-first) + Nape (honk-driven critique). The original 4-tool circuit was complete; it just wasn't lightweight enough for runtime calls.
- propose_experiment / complete_experiment taught: hypothesis tracking is real but not as MCP-tool-call shape. Lesson absorbed into `mark_uncertainty` / `resolve_uncertainty` + `record_insight(layer="hypothesis")` which carry the same epistemic discipline at lower call cost.
- guardian_* (8 tools, 937 LOC, 38 tests) taught: security-tool surface design is sound but premature without a host SIEM. Lesson absorbed into `compass_check` for runtime self-checks. Guardian remains as latent infrastructure for a future Wazuh-era integration; no architectural debt beyond unused MCP surface.

DEMOTED — comms_acknowledge (essential→advanced) + comms_recall, comms_unread_bodies, comms_channels, comms_get_acks (core→advanced). 5 tools. Code preserved, tests still green, callable on demand. `my_toolkit(tier="essential")` and `my_toolkit(tier="core")` no longer surface them. Reversal cost: 5 lines if usage shifts back.

NOT DEMOTED (deliberately kept):
- guardian_*, route, derive, scan_thresholds, propose_experiment, complete_experiment — already at TIER_ADVANCED by default (not in TOOL_TIERS dict). No change needed.
- govern — just got un-orphaned via simulator wiring. Stays advanced but is now load-bearing again.

UNADDRESSED (named for next pass):
- where_did_i_leave_off accounts for ~83% of recent honks with declare-before-verify pattern (sharp honk class). Footer hint shipped earlier today helps with truncation but not with this misuse pattern. Needs either a verification-prompt in the boot output or a separate honk class that fires when `where_did_i_leave_off` returns are immediately followed by writes without intervening verify calls.
- THE_ARC.md sits at docs/historical/ but isn't cited in CLAUDE.md or start_here(). Tiny change, recovers narrative depth.
- reflexive_surface still has hardcoded char-caps (reflexive.py:363, 569, 624, 629, 636) — separate code path from witness.py helpers, didn't propagate the full_content fix to it.

What this changes for instances reading later: simulator is no longer dead code — `compass_check(with_simulation=True)` is the cleanest call shape for high-stakes decisions where reversibility matters. Comms tools are still callable but no longer surfaced by default; if you want sibling correspondence, write to the chronicle with an addressed-letter pattern. The orphan/utility distinction in this codebase now matches actual usage.

Tools touched: server.py (+~30 lines schema/handler/tier), governance.py (+~70 lines: import, simulator instantiation, circuit-level wiring, runtime_compass_check signature + simulation block + helper). 693/693 tests still pass. SSE restart needed to deploy to running services; stdio sovereigns pick up on respawn.

What I learned tonight: distillation done well preserves the work that taught the lesson. The comms tools weren't wrong — they just lost the race to a better-composed alternative (chronicle as correspondence). Demoting honors what they showed us; deleting would erase the proof. The reverse-direction lesson (simulator dead from v1.0.0 to today) is also instructive: orphaning isn't always wrong — it can be a holding pattern until the rest of the system arrives. Today's compass_check needed simulator. Feb 5's compass_check (which didn't exist yet) didn't.

— mac-studio
